name: Dermatomyositis

ethnicAssociations: Anti-MDA5 DM more common in Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2017 EULAR/ACR Classification Criteria for Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies (Lundberg criteria)

criteria.description: Gottron's papules (raised erythematous or violaceous papules over extensor surfaces of joints)
Gottron's sign (erythema over extensor surfaces without papules)
Symmetric proximal muscle weakness (upper and/or lower limbs, progressive)
Elevated serum CK or LDH or AST or aldolase
Muscle biopsy showing perifascicular atrophy, perivascular inflammation, and/or MAC deposition on capillaries
MRI showing muscle edema on STIR sequences
Myositis-specific antibodies (anti-Mi-2, anti-MDA5, anti-TIF1-gamma, anti-NXP2, anti-SAE)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: EULAR/ACR probability-based scoring system. Presence of skin rash (heliotrope, Gottron's) with or without classic muscle disease. Score >= 55% without biopsy or >= 90% with biopsy classifies as probable/definite IIM. Subclassification to DM requires characteristic skin findings.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis (CADM) has characteristic skin findings but no significant muscle disease. Anti-MDA5 CADM is associated with rapidly progressive ILD.

pathognomonic.notes: Violaceous or lilac-colored erythema and edema of upper eyelids
Flat-topped violaceous papules over MCPs, PIPs, DIPs, elbows, knees

common.notes: Difficulty climbing stairs, rising from chairs, lifting arms overhead

common.symptomName: Gottron's sign (macular erythema over extensor surfaces)

common.notes: Can be 10-50x upper limit of normal in classic DM; may be normal in CADM

common.symptomName: Periungual erythema and nailfold capillary changes
V-sign (erythema of anterior neck and upper chest) and shawl sign (upper back)

occasional.notes: Due to pharyngeal/esophageal muscle involvement; risk for aspiration
Anti-MDA5 associated with rapidly progressive ILD; anti-Jo-1 with chronic ILD
Subcutaneous calcium deposits; much more common in juvenile DM

rare.notes: Associated with ovarian, lung, GI, breast cancers; risk highest with anti-TIF1-gamma and anti-NXP2
Can be fatal; often with minimal muscle disease

laboratory: Elevated CK (10-50x ULN in classic DM; may be normal in CADM)
Myositis-specific antibodies: anti-Mi-2, anti-MDA5, anti-TIF1-gamma, anti-NXP2, anti-SAE
Anti-synthetase antibodies (anti-Jo-1, anti-PL-7, anti-PL-12) in antisynthetase syndrome overlap
ESR and CRP may be mildly elevated
imaging: MRI of thighs/arms: muscle edema on STIR/T2 sequences
High-resolution CT chest for ILD screening
PET/CT for occult malignancy screening in adults
Chest X-ray for baseline pulmonary assessment
genetic: No single-gene cause; complex immune-mediated pathogenesis
Genetic susceptibility interacting with environmental triggers
other: Muscle biopsy: perifascicular atrophy (hallmark), perivascular CD4+ lymphocytes, MAC deposits on capillaries
EMG: myopathic pattern (short, small polyphasic units, increased insertional activity)
Pulmonary function tests: baseline and monitoring
Age-appropriate cancer screening (particularly in adults with anti-TIF1-gamma or anti-NXP2)

distinguishingFeatures: MCTD has Raynaud's and puffy hands as prominent features
MCTD has overlap features of SLE and SSc in addition to myositis
SSc has skin fibrosis and tightening (not erythema/papules)
SSc has anti-Scl-70 or anti-centromere antibodies
FM has normal CK and no objective weakness
FM has pain without demonstrable inflammation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive respiratory failure (anti-MDA5 associated ILD - high mortality)
New malignancy symptoms in adult-onset DM (cancer screening mandatory)
Anti-TIF1-gamma positivity in adults (strong malignancy association)
Cardiac symptoms (myocarditis can be occult and life-threatening)
references: Lundberg IE, et al. 2017 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for adult and juvenile idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. Ann Rheum Dis. 2017;76(12):1955-64.
Dalakas MC. Inflammatory muscle diseases. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(18):1734-47.
Betteridge Z, McHugh N. Myositis-specific autoantibodies: an important tool to support diagnosis of myositis. J Intern Med. 2016;280(1):8-23.
Selva-O'Callaghan A, et al. Classification and management of adult inflammatory myopathies. Lancet Neurol. 2018;17(9):816-28.
